newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHORT YIELDS COULD RISE IF BFR STAYS WEAK.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHORT YIELDS COULD RISE IF BFR STAYS WEAK.

text.p: Belgian short-term interest rates could rise if the Belgian franc remains at its relatively weak level of 20.64 to the mark, dealers said on Tuesday.

The franc ended at 20.6405/15 to the mark, well above its 20.6255 ERM midpoint, continuing a gentle slide which started mid-April and brought the currency back to the lows seen in February. It closed at 20.6400/10 Monday.

"The market is not worried, and yields even tend to fall rather than rise, but if the spot rate remains at 20.64 for a long time, short-time rates will come under upward pressure," said Bacob chief dealer Johan Evenepoel.
Dealers said they saw no reason for the franc to be so weak and that the central bank was still giving ample liquidity at repo rates around 3.08 percent.

One noted that the Treasury had sold 118 billion francs worth of T-bills today, while just 53 billion was at expiry. "Maybe the state wanted to be sure of some cheap funding for the weeks ahead," he said. The three-month auction yield was 3.21 percent, from 3.22 percent last week.
At the OLO exchange auction the Treasury exchanged 33.75 billion francs of paper, of which 24.34 billion in OLO 15 which matures this month.
Dealers said the market was now waiting for U.S. April PPI on Wednesday (seen at 1.5 percent year-on-year) and CPI on Thursday (seen at 2.6 percent).
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
